rationale: Lyc action-noun ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- (= ⲧⲟⲓⲛ-) on the verbal phrase ⲣ̄-ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'go out forth.' The chapter title and enumerated list make this the technical Manichaean term for each of the Five cosmic Redemptions/Liberations of the Light. Distinct from ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲛⲟⲩϩⲙⲉ 'the saving' and ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ 'the raising,' which appear paired with it as constitutive aspects.
Lyc action-noun ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- on ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' (per terminology rule, retain vertical semantics). The first half of the dyad 'raising and saving' that defines each Going-Forth.
Lyc action-noun on ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙⲉ/ⲛⲁϩⲙ̄ 'save, rescue.' Second half of the redemption-dyad with ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ.

Lycopolitan verbal phrase 'to be king over.' ϩⲟⲣⲟ likely a dialectal infinitive of ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ (cf. Lyc ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ already in vocab) with prosthetic ϩ-onset. The directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'upon him/it' completes the construction. Distinct from ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'the king' (line 12), which is the same root substantivized.
Lycopolitan plural of ⲟⲁⲙ/ⲟⲩⲁⲙ = Sahidic ϫⲟⲙ 'power, might.' Already attested in vocab as ⲛⲟⲁⲙ 'might/strength' but here clearly plural in 'all the powers of the Darkness.'
Greek ἀρχοντική (substantivized fem.) 'the archonic [power/realm].' Standard Manichaean technical term for the collective body of archons whose grip the First Man's Light is saved from.
Privative ⲛⲁⲧ- + ϯϣ 'measure' + ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'to it' = 'without giving measure to it' = immeasurable. Standard Coptic construction; modifies ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'light' here in the context of the Second Going-Forth.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲡⲓⲱⲧ. The ⲛ for ⲓ is a known dialectal spelling. Restored in line 16 as the speaker of the kephalaion's exposition.
